title: What's New in Kotlin Jump
tagline: Coroutine clarity, readable @Suppress, full-column nav history
summary: Three changes: coroutine builders now carry dispatcher badges (🧵 IO · 🖥 Main · ⚙ Default), every @Suppress / @SuppressLint / @SuppressWarnings ID explains itself on hover, and Cmd+Alt+←/→ finally restores the exact column across navigation jumps — in every language, not just Kotlin/Java.

highlights.title: Dispatcher badges on coroutine builders
highlights.description: Any withContext(Dispatchers.X), launch(Dispatchers.X), async(Dispatchers.X), or flowOn(Dispatchers.X) now shows an inline badge — 🧵 IO, 🖥 Main, ⚙ Default, or 🔀 Unconfined — so you see which thread the block runs on without scrolling up. The ⚡ suspend marker still appears on every suspend call.
highlights.mediaAlt: Suspend call markers with dispatcher badges inline

highlights.title: @Suppress / @SuppressLint explained on hover
highlights.description: Hover any ID inside @Suppress("UNCHECKED_CAST") or @SuppressLint("MissingPermission") to see a plain-English description of what the warning means, its category, and a link to the official docs. Ships with ~40 of the most common Kotlin, Android Lint, and javac suppression IDs. Multi-argument annotations work too — every ID is independently hoverable.
highlights.mediaAlt: Hover tooltip showing a plain-English explanation of a suppression ID

highlights.title: Cmd+Alt+←/→ now restores the exact column, everywhere
highlights.description: The README has advertised Cmd+Alt+←/→ as navigation history since day one, but the shortcut was never bound — users hit VS Code's native navigateBack, which only restores files, not the column. v1.16.0 ships the binding. Works in every editor, every language, every file type — not just Kotlin/Java. Your exact cursor position (line AND column) is now preserved across every jump.

sections.heading: New features
bullets: Dispatcher badges on withContext / launch / async / flowOn / produce / actor when they receive Dispatchers.IO / .Main / .Main.immediate / .Default / .Unconfined as a direct argument. Inline hints are synchronous and regex-based — no dataflow — so assigning a dispatcher to a variable first still renders as a plain call.

Hover on any ID inside @Suppress(...), @SuppressLint(...), or @SuppressWarnings(...) shows a short description, the category (Kotlin / Android Lint / javac), and a doc link. Unknown IDs stay silent rather than noisy.

Cmd+Alt+← / Cmd+Alt+→ (Ctrl+Alt on Windows/Linux) are now bound to Kotlin Jump's column-restoring navigation history in every editor. VS Code's native navigateBack only restores the file — the new binding restores line AND column across jumps. The binding is only active when an editor has focus, so terminals, sidebars, and the command palette keep their native behavior.

Shift+Alt+I toggles every inline annotation Kotlin Jump ships — string-resource folding, color swatches, const-val folding, !! highlights, hex swatches — in one keystroke. Useful for screenshots, pair programming, or catching a regression behind the overlay.
Shift+Alt+C copies the fully-qualified name of the symbol under the cursor in Kotlin and Java files. Pastes `com.example.pkg.Class.method` straight into a ticket, chat, or search.

sections.heading: Notes
bullets: The README previously advertised dispatcher badges and the Cmd+Alt+←/→ shortcut as already existing; v1.16.0 finally makes both features match the documentation. If you were confused by their absence in earlier releases, this release closes the gap.
The dispatcher badges and @Suppress hover are lightweight — pure regex plus a static dictionary. No new workers, no new indexes, no measurable cost at scan time.
